safe_price_bound = 2^62-1 defined in theories/Trading.v; max_profit_fits_i64 / max_drawdown_fits_i64 closed under the global context (Print Assumptions); python/rocq.py SAFE_PRICE_BOUND mirrors it and _enforce_price_domain rejects with DomainError citing the theorem.
step computes `pos + qty` before range-checking; step_fits_i64 states the extra obligation limit + max|qty| <= i64_max; enforced in python/rocq.py run_orders.
run_orders_within_limit assumes -lim <= pos0 <= lim; python/rocq.py rejects limit < 0 (empty interval) and initial outside [-limit, limit] with ValueError before calling native code.
python/demo.py section 5: max_profit([-SAFE_PRICE_BOUND, SAFE_PRICE_BOUND]) = 9223372036854775806 matches the Python spec transliteration exactly at the proved boundary.

python/demo.py: 2000 random series vs naive O(n^2) spec for max_profit and max_drawdown, 2000 random order sequences vs naive gate, plus 2000 random sort lists vs sorted(); rust/trading_main.rs repeats this natively with 5000 trials. All pass as of this audit's toolchain.

rust/rocq_ffi/src/lib.rs wraps every call into extracted code in catch_unwind; status codes ROCQ_OK/ROCQ_ERR_NULL/ROCQ_ERR_PANIC; quiet panic hook with ROCQ_FFI_VERBOSE opt-out; demo layer-1 test observes RocqError instead of a crash.
python/rocq.py rejects float (TypeError, bool excluded via isinstance check), out-of-int64 (OverflowError); demo.py section 4 exercises all three rejections.
README section 'What is still trusted' names: extraction pretty-printer, remap table, FFI marshalling + ctypes packing, rustc/cargo.
